paper_title: DIY-MKG An LLM-Based Polyglot Language Learning System
caption: DIY-MKG reliably expands the vocabulary with low sensitivity to the language and the starting word. For each language, 10 opaque curves represent vocabulary sizes obtained from 10 different starting words, and one solid curve represents the average of the 10 curves. The standard deviations across languages and starting words are small, indicating fairness for all language learners. The diagonal gray line represents the upper-bound of vocabulary size, assuming all words in each iteration have not yet appeared in the vocabulary. While the real expansion rate is lower, the vocabulary does not saturate after 500 iterations. Therefore, DIY-MKG can reliably help the language learner to expand their vocabulary by consistently introducing new words.
model_annotation: The plot illustrates the growth of vocabulary size over the number of iterations for three languages—Spanish, Korean, and Japanese—using the DIY-MKG system. The x-axis represents the number of iterations, ranging from 0 to 500 on a linear scale, with tick marks at intervals of 100. The y-axis represents vocabulary size, ranging from 0 to 5000 on a linear scale, with tick marks at intervals of 1000. For each language, ten translucent curves (blue for Spanish, orange for Korean, green for Japanese) depict vocabulary sizes obtained from ten different starting words, while a solid curve of the same color represents the average across these ten runs. All three average curves show a consistent upward trend, starting at 0 and reaching approximately 3000 by 500 iterations, with the Spanish curve slightly above the others and the Japanese curve slightly below. The shaded regions around each average curve indicate variability, and the small spread suggests low sensitivity to the starting word and language. A diagonal gray line, representing the theoretical upper bound (where every word introduced in each iteration is novel), rises from (0,0) to (500,5000), indicating that the actual vocabulary growth is lower but still substantial and non-saturating over 500 iterations.
